subject: Archaeology
title: Stonehenge: The Mystery That Won't Die
description: Learn Stonehenge: The Mystery That Won't Die in one minute.

hook.text: Stonehenge took 1,500 years to build. The biggest stones weigh 25 tons and were dragged 25 miles to the site.

buildup.text: The smaller bluestones came from Wales — 150 miles away. How they were transported remains one of archaeology's biggest puzzles.

discovery.text: The stones align with the sunrise on the summer solstice and sunset on the winter solstice — a deliberate solar calendar.

twist.text: Cremated remains of over 60 people were buried at Stonehenge. It was also a cemetery — not just an observatory.

climax.text: Chemical analysis of the bones shows people came from as far as Wales and the Mediterranean to be buried there.

punchline.text: People traveled hundreds of miles to be buried at Stonehenge.

quiz.question: What did analysis of cremated remains at Stonehenge reveal?
options: All burials were local farmers from the Salisbury Plain
People came from as far as Wales and the Mediterranean to be buried there
Only royalty and priests were allowed to be interred at the site

details.summary: Stonehenge in England was built in stages between 3000 and 2000 BCE. Its massive sarsen stones were transported from 25 miles away and its bluestones from Wales, 150 miles distant. Despite centuries of study, its precise purpose — astronomical observatory, temple, or healing site — remains debated.
details.whyItMatters: Stonehenge embodies the enduring mystery of the past. It demonstrates that Neolithic Britons possessed engineering skills, astronomical knowledge, and social organization far beyond what was long assumed for prehistoric societies.
takeaways: Stonehenge was built between 3000 and 2000 BCE in stages
Bluestones were transported 150 miles from Wales
Its purpose remains debated despite centuries of study

faq.question: How were Stonehenge's massive stones moved?
faq.answer: The sarsen stones (up to 25 tons) were likely dragged on sledges and rollers from Marlborough Downs. The bluestones (up to 4 tons) may have come from Wales by a combination of land and water transport, though some geologists argue glaciers moved them partway.

faq.question: Is Stonehenge aligned with the sun?
faq.answer: Yes. The main axis aligns with sunrise on the summer solstice and sunset on the winter solstice. This alignment was clearly intentional, though whether Stonehenge functioned as a full astronomical observatory or simply marked key solar events is still debated.
